abstract: TIGR-Tas system holds great promise for genome-engineering applications owing to its compact size and PAMless targeting capability. However, its low editing efficiency in mammalian cells severely limits its broader utility. Here, we engineered a highly active variant of ParTasR, termed eTasR, through structure-guided rational design of ParTasR combined with fusion to the exonuclease TREX2. eTasR increased mammalian editing efficiency from the original 4.29% to 48.94% with an average 26.52-fold increase, significantly surpassing the efficiency of SpRY, a reported version of PAM-free nuclease. More importantly, single-AAV delivery enabled efficient Hpd disruption in vivo, resulting in robust phenotypic rescue. Thus, eTasR provides a compact, PAMless and highly efficient platform for genome editing and therapeutic applications.
